title: Cap. X Arg. X close toward Corvinus: opposite for the elect — eternal saving will proves election/preterition; foresight cannot ground either special will or its denial
pass_a_gloss: just as on the contrary, as concerns those who are made religious, faithful, persevering, and are led unto everlasting life, we can gather that from eternity that will was present unto God which would efficaciously work all these things in them. But this will of saving, and non-will (if one may so speak) manifestly proves the election of some and the preterition of others. Finally, just as it would be inept to pretend that this special will of working faith, perseverance, and salvation in Peter flowed from foresight of the same Peter’s faith and perseverance, so it is no less false and inept to assert that this denied will of effecting faith, repentance, and perseverance in Judas, or in any reprobate, had its origin from foresight of the same man’s unbelief, impenitence, and final contempt of Divine grace.
pass_b_english: Conversely, of those made religious, faithful, persevering, and led to everlasting life, we may gather that from eternity God had that will which would efficaciously work all this in them. That will to save—and non-will, if one may so speak—plainly proves election of some and preterition of others. Finally: as it would be inept to claim that the special will to work faith, perseverance, and salvation in Peter flowed from foresight of Peter’s faith and perseverance, so it is no less false and inept to assert that the denied will to effect faith, repentance, and perseverance in Judas or any reprobate arose from foresight of his unbelief, impenitence, and final contempt of divine grace.
source_text: sicut e contra, quoad eos qui religiosi, fideles, perseverantes efficiuntur, et ad vitam aeternam perducuntur, colligere possumus ab aeterno adfuisse Deo illam voluntatem, quae haec omnia in illis efficaciter operaretur. Haec autem voluntas salvandi, et noluntas (si ita loqui liceat) electionem aliquorum et praeteritionem aliorum manifeste evincit. Denique, sicut ineptum esset obtendere hanc specialem voluntatem de fide, perseverantia et salute Petri operanda ex praevisa ejusdem Petri fide et perseverantia profluxisse, ita non minus falsum et ineptum est asserere, hanc negatam voluntatem efficiendi fidem, poenitentiam et perseverantiam in Juda, aut quolibet reprobato, ex praevisa ejusdem infidelitate, impoenitentia et finali gratiae Divinae contemptu originem habuisse.
